cs.t: "The world got more benefit from c64s and vic20s" I started coding in 1981 on an VC20, learned a lot from it, but wonder how did the world benefit more from vic20s? As a happy smartphone user, I think the world did benefit a lot e.g. from the Newton (loved mine, dropped a Palm for it, sad it died, but it was too heavy).
I loved the Newton in all forms, both the tiny laptop which I consider the Pocket Reform to be a development on, and the handheld pdas. Keeping it alive is very important.
cs.th: Einstein: NewtonOS running on other operating systems

cs.t: Not really; I have pretty much the "standard" keyboard for each of a bunch of systems. The most interesting thing about them is the range of variability in quality. Some of that is survivorship bias, but I think it's remarkable that the Newton MP2000's keyboard works at all -- as far as Apple products go, it looks like a product of the middle Mac age but feels like the worst membrane HP ever shipped with their bottom-range consumer PCs.
The EL backlight adds to the slightly unearthly vibe too. The eMate was one of the last mainstream laptop-size devices made with an EL backlight. I miss those.
cs.th: Einstein: NewtonOS running on other operating systems

cs.t: The Newton had an absolutely brilliant user interface, but its hardware let it down. I wish we had a device similar to the smaller Remarkable tablet, running something like NewtonOS. (Related: Columbo's Mystery Capers is an amazing and hilarious game from one of the Zork devs that has never been dumped and doesn't exist on any other platform. I hope someone will figure out how to get it off an actual Newton and get it to run on Einstein.)
cs.th: Einstein: NewtonOS running on other operating systems
